messages:
maria: heads up, canary shows a 12-18% tail latency bump after the prefill/decode batching split landed. not universal but spikes on medium request sizes (seq len 384-768).

jon: saw that too. spikes mostly at p95-p99 on the 8-GPU pool. throughput unchanged.

ashwin: digging into profiler now. initial hunch: kernel-channel mismatch during decode phase leads to extra kernel churn. also KV eviction noise. profiling snippet: 
```
profile: decode_phase_kernel_switches: +42%
profile: kv-cache-evictions/sec: 3.8 -> 9.7
profile: batch-formation-time-ms: 1.2 -> 1.9
```

lisa: thanks. do we have a repro trace with request ids? canary traces?

maria: yes pushing one to stackdriver: projects/redwood/canary/trace/trace-4305000000. top-level symptom: many small decode batches (4-8 tokens) interleaved with large prefill batches -> kernel selection thrash.

jon: that explains kernel churn. when decoder batch < kernel-optimal-min, we pick a slow kernel. then next prefill forces a different kernel and we context-switch.

ashwin: also saw KV priming failing for split flows: prefill used warm KV, decode got cold cache because we flush between stage-queues in new split policy. eviction TTL looks too aggressive.

maria: linking the fallback policy we rolled: split_queues=true, handshake_window_ms=10, token_budget_target=64. maybe handshake window too tight for our latency tail.

lisa: what if handshake_window_ms=30 and token_budget_target=96 for these medium sequences? reduces early decode batching and lets KV stay warm.

jon: +1 to increasing handshake, but we should be careful for sub-100ms latency SLOs. propose canary with handshake_window_ms=30 & token_budget_target=96 on half of canary nodes.

perf-bot: deploy plan generated: canary/phase-split-adjust -> 6 nodes, percentage: 50%, expected metrics to watch: p50/p95/p99 latency, kv-evictions/sec, kernel-switches/sec, tokens/sec.

maria: quick patch proposal: 
- increase handshake_window_ms to 30ms
- token_budget_target=96 for seq_len 384-768 bucket only (keep default for small/huge)
- if kernel_switches/sec > 20% baseline, auto-fallback to combined batching for that pool

ashwin: adding to that: relax KV eviction TTL by +50% when split_queues=true for the bucket to avoid cold decode.

jon: can we add a hotspot metric on "decode-small-batches-%" and alert if > 15% for more than 5m? helps auto-detect regression.

lisa: agree. also add a short-lived perf regression test in CI that simulates mixed prefill+decode interleaving at medium length to catch this earlier.

maria: I'll open a canary and post patch. deploy-bot will run the rollout. ping me if numbers look worse.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: canary/phase-split-adjust -> nodes: 6 -> 3 updated. expected completion: 10m.

ashwin: one more datapoint from trace: kernel warmup penalty ~2.1ms on first decode kernel call after prefill switch. multiplied across many requests this accounts for most of the increase.

jon: ok if warmup penalty is primary, then batching policy should prefer keeping decode kernels hot. that matches handshake window increase.

maria: postmortem checklist item: document tradeoffs of split_queues default and bucket thresholds. also capture heuristics for when auto-fallback should trigger.

lisa: i'll add a short doc to the runbook and a dashboard widget called "split-batch-health" with charts: kernel-switch-rate, kv-evictions, decode-small-batches-%, p99 latency.

maria: canary update in 12m, will post numbers. thanks all. :thumbsup:
